[02] At a glance

Two kinds of roofing customer. Two clocks.

Homeowners decide in days, often after a storm. Commercial buyers decide in months, with approvals.

Roofing: Residential vs Commercial
RESIDENTIALCOMMERCIAL
Who buysHomeowners, often right after a stormProperty managers, HOAs, facility teams
What starts itStorm damage, an old roof, a home saleBudgets, inspections, a bid request
Sales cycleDays to a few weeksMonths, with approvals
What winsA fast inspection, reviews, a clear claim explanationComplete bids, references, maintenance programs
Ticket$[ ] per re-roof$[ ] per project, plus programs

02/ 10ROOFING

[03] Residential

Homeowners hire the roofer they trust first.

Re-roofs, storm repairs and insurance claims are big, stressful decisions. Trust is built before the inspection and confirmed after it.

REVIEWS AND TRUST

[4.9] ★ · [212] reviews

Your rating, shown where homeowners decide.

What reviews should mention after every job

  • Re-roofs

    Planned replacements on aging roofs, often timed with a sale or a renovation.

    They need: options, a clear price, financing

  • Storm damage & insurance claims

    Hail and wind damage that has to be documented before the claim.

    They need: a fast inspection and a plain explanation of the claim

  • Inspections

    The free inspection is the first yes. It starts every residential job.

    They need: an easy time slot and photos afterwards

[04] Commercial

Commercial roofs are won over months, not calls.

Property managers, HOAs and facility teams buy through bids, approvals and references. We keep you in the process at every step.

  • Property managers
  • HOAs
  • Facilities
  1. WEEK 0Bid requestFrom a PM, an HOA board or a facility manager
  2. WEEK 1Site walkMeasurements, core samples, photos
  3. WEEKS 2–3Proposal & bidScope, options, warranty, references
  4. WEEKS 4–8Board or owner approvalFollow-up that answers questions, not just checks in
  5. WEEK 9Contract signedScheduled around tenants and weather
  6. AFTERMaintenance programTwo inspections a year, repairs before leaks

04/ 10ROOFING

[05] Only in roofing · Storm season

The first 72 hours after a storm decide the season.

Insurance-driven demand moves fast. The roofers who are visible, bookable and clear about claims in the first days get most of the inspections.

Hour 0
Hour 0Drag the clock →Week 2+

After the storm

  1. Hour 0Hail reported. We watch storm reports for your service area; when hail or high wind hits your ZIP codes, the plan starts.
  2. Hour 1Storm pages live. Landing pages and ads for the affected areas, with your reviews and claim help.
  3. Hour 2Booking open. Homeowners pick an inspection time online; reminders go out automatically.
  4. Days 1–3Inspections. Crews inspect, photograph and document the damage for the claim.
  5. Week 2+Claims & proposals. Proposals followed up until the roof is signed.
